matrices.title: DNA Polymerase I vs. DNA Polymerase III
matrices.summary: Comparison of the two primary replicative DNA polymerases in Escherichia coli.
rows: Primary Replicative Role
Removes RNA primers and fills the resulting gaps on the lagging strand; DNA repair [L2 p16]
Primary replicative enzyme responsible for continuous leading strand and discontinuous lagging strand synthesis [L2 p15]
5' -> 3' Polymerase Activity
**Present** (rate: ~16-20 nucleotides/sec; moderate processivity ~3-200 nucleotides) [L2 p12]
**Present** (rate: ~250-1000 nucleotides/sec; extremely high processivity >500,000 nucleotides via beta clamp) [L2 p12, 15]
3' -> 5' Exonuclease Activity
**Present** (proofreading: removes mispaired terminal 3' nucleotides) [L2 p12, 14]
**Present** in epsilon subunit (proofreading: ensures high fidelity replication ~1 error per 10^7 nucleotides) [L2 p12, 14]
5' -> 3' Exonuclease Activity
**Present** (unique: enables **Nick Translation** to degrade RNA primers or damaged DNA in front of the enzyme) [L2 p12, 16]
**Absent** entirely [L2 p12]
Subunit Composition
Single monomeric polypeptide (~103 kDa; can be proteolytically cleaved into Klenow fragment + small exonuclease domain) [L2 p12]
Asymmetric heteromultimeric holoenzyme (10 distinct subunits: catalytic core alpha-epsilon-theta, beta sliding clamp dimer, gamma-tau clamp loader complex) [L2 p15]

matrices.title: DNA Replication: Prokaryotes vs. Eukaryotes
matrices.summary: Key mechanistic and structural differences between bacterial and eukaryotic replication machinery.
rows: Origin of Replication
Single unique origin per circular chromosome (OriC, 245 bp) [L2 p6]
Multiple origins of replication per linear chromosome (thousands of replication bubbles spaced 30-300 kb apart) [L2 p25]
Replication Fork Movement
Bidirectional from single origin; two forks meet at Ter termination sites [L2 p6, 22]
Bidirectional from multiple origins simultaneously [L2 p25]
Primary Replicative Polymerases
DNA Polymerase III (elongation); DNA Polymerase I (primer removal) [L2 p12, 15]
Pol alpha (primase complex: synthesizes RNA/DNA primer); Pol delta (lagging strand); Pol epsilon (leading strand) [L2 p26, 28]
Sliding Clamp & Loader
Beta clamp homodimer; gamma-tau complex clamp loader [L2 p15]
PCNA (Proliferating Cell Nuclear Antigen) trimer; RFC (Replication Factor C) loader [L2 p28]
Primer Removal
DNA Polymerase I (5' -> 3' exonuclease nick translation) [L2 p16]
RNase H hydrolyzes RNA; FEN1 (Flap Endonuclease 1) cleaves displaced flap [L2 p29]
End-Replication Problem & Telomeres
Non-existent: Chromosome is circular, no free ends [L2 p4]
Linear chromosome ends would shorten with each round; resolved by Telomerase (reverse transcriptase with internal RNA template TTAGGG) [L2 p32, 33]

matrices.title: Major DNA Repair Pathways
matrices.summary: Comparison of cellular mechanisms correcting damaged or mismatched DNA.
rows: Direct Reversal [L3 p6, 8]
Pyrimidine dimers (photolyase in bacteria) or O6-methylguanine (alkyl damage) [L3 p6, 8]
O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT): Transfers methyl group directly from O6-guanine to internal cysteine residue (suicide enzyme) [L3 p8]
Chemotherapy resistance (high MGMT expression protects tumor cells from alkylating agents like temozolomide) [L3 p8]
Base Excision Repair (BER) [L3 p10-14]
Single abnormal/modified bases: Deaminated cytosine (uracil in DNA), oxidized guanine (8-oxoG), alkylated bases [L3 p10]
1. DNA Glycosylase cleaves N-glycosidic bond, creating AP site; 2. AP Endonuclease cleaves 5' phosphodiester bond; 3. DNA Pol I (or Pol beta) fills gap, DNA ligase seals [L3 p11-13]
MUTYH-associated polyposis (colorectal adenomas caused by defective 8-oxoG repair) [L3 p14]
Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER) [L3 p15-22]
Bulky helix-distorting lesions: UV-induced cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers (CPD) and 6-4 photoproducts; chemical adducts [L3 p15]

1. UvrABC excinuclease (prokaryotes) or XPA-XPG complexes (eukaryotes) make dual incisions flanking lesion (12-29 nt); 2. Helicase releases damaged oligomer; 3. DNA Pol and Ligase resynthesize [L3 p16-18]
Xeroderma Pigmentosum (XP): Extreme UV sensitivity, severe sunburns, marked increase in skin carcinomas and melanomas [L3 p20]
Mismatch Repair (MMR) [L3 p23-28]
Post-replicative replication errors: Base-base mismatches and small insertion/deletion loops that escaped proofreading [L3 p23]
1. MutS binds mismatch, MutL coordinates, MutH cleaves unmethylated daughter strand at GATC sites; 2. Exonuclease degrades past lesion; 3. Pol III fills and Ligase seals [L3 p24-26]
Lynch Syndrome (Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colorectal Cancer / HNPCC): Germline mutation in MSH2 or MLH1 causes microsatellite instability [L3 p28]
